title: Adaptive ingress throttling + soft-priority aging to resolve KV-cache churn and queue starvation on mixed workloads
creator: Maya Patel
description: Two production escalations (Acme Finance on Dedicated, NovaChat on Hosted) exposed an intermittent but recurring failure mode where large long-context requests repeatedly evicted KV cache entries and starved latency-sensitive small requests. Symptoms: 99th percentile tail latency for small chat completions spiked from ~120ms to 4-9s during sustained long-request bursts; cache eviction rate increased ~7x; scheduler queue depth grew and small requests experienced head-of-line delays for several seconds. This ticket tracks the engineering work to implement adaptive ingress throttling, soft-priority aging, and a conservative preemption path across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private modes, plus rollout/ops runbook updates and monitoring additions.
reproduction_steps: Create mixed workload with 80% small short-context requests (~8-20 tokens infer) and 20% long-context requests (2k-8k tokens).
Send long-context requests as bursts (10-20 concurrent) repeatedly over a 60s window to a single serving pool.
Observe: batch scheduler stalls forming large heterogeneous batches, KV cache eviction rate spikes, small request p99 latency climbs.
Use dev cluster with matching kernels/quantization to reproduce exact eviction patterns (see runbook link).
root_cause_summary: The batch scheduler admitted long-context requests without accounting for their disproportionate compute and KV-cache working set impact. The admission controller used only queue-depth and token-count heuristics which undercounted effective cost for long-context requests (KV footprin​t + attention complexity). As long requests entered the pool, they triggered KV eviction churn and increased per-batch runtime; scheduler then formed large heterogeneous batches that blocked small low-latency flows (head-of-line blocking). Additionally, the lack of request aging meant low-priority small requests could be indefinitely delayed behind repeated large bursts.
mitigation: Hotfix: set conservative per-pool concurrent long-request cap and enforce a 1s soft window between admitting new long-context requests (canaryed on Dedicated pool A).
Rollback knob: manual scale-up to burst-capacity pools for affected customers (ops playbook updated).
Customer-facing: opened incidents with Acme Finance and NovaChat; provided temporary route-mirroring and traffic shaping suggestions for clients using single-pool pins.
fix_summary: Implement an adaptive admission cost model that estimates request cost = tokens * attention_factor + estimated KV working set. Add soft-priority aging so small latency-sensitive requests accrue priority weight while waiting. Add a lightweight preemption hook: if a batch is about to execute and contains small requests older than X ms, try to split the batch or move the small requests into a separate fast lane. Provide configuration flags for Hosted (default conservative), Dedicated (tenant override), and Private (operator upgrade notes).
rollout_plan: 2) Canary: roll to 5% of Dedicated pools (non-production customers) for 48h, monitor p50/p95/p99 for small flows and KV eviction rate.
3) Gradual increase to customer-facing Dedicated pools for affected Acme Finance region with a fallback toggle.
4) For Hosted: enable default conservative mode behind feature flag for 24h canary then full enable.
5) Private: publish operator upgrade notes and a CLI flag to enable adaptive admission; recommend testing in staging with retained KV cache diagnostic hooks.
acceptance_criteria: Small-request p99 latency returns to within 20% of baseline under mixed workload tests in staging (synthetic replay).
KV eviction rate reduces to <=2x baseline under equivalent long-request burst workloads in perf lab.
No more than 3% throughput regression for long-context requests in Dedicated canary pools (documented tradeoff).
Feature flags exist for Hosted default, Dedicated tenant override, and Private operator enable; upgrade docs published.
Automated integration tests added to verify aging and preemption logic under synthetic heterogeneous batches.
